- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline at 1–2% below recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model underestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term volatility — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ true values.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model delays correction — add 1–2 days lag in downward adjustment.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to forecast higher than true — subtract 2–5% from forecast mean.
- Model often ignores sentiment trend — if sentiment is trending downward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 7 days.
